uzo.purpose: Shows a symbol from the brand's icon set, decorative by default, named when it carries meaning.

instead.kialo: A status needs a word, because colour and a shape alone are no information for everyone (WCAG 1.4.1) and a picture is not read aloud; the insigno says the status in one to three words, with an icon beside it if the Aspekto wants one.

A logo is the picture of a brand, not a sign of the system, because it keeps its own colours and proportions and never takes the text's colour; it belongs to the Aspekto as an asset of its own, which Fundamento does not carry yet.

boundary.kialo: A picture outside the Ikonaro has no name in the core, because every name is vocabulary every Aspekto draws (Art. IV); a person decides whether the Ikonaro grows by a name or the picture is content.
An icon is still, because motion is a state of an Ero (the loading plenstato turns its indicator) and not of a sign; a sign that moves would carry meaning the name does not.

with.kialo: A button shows an icon before or after its label, or alone with a label prop, because the sign shortens what the word says; the icon takes the button's colour and size.
A notice shows the icon of its intent beside its words, because a sign is read faster than a word — and never alone, the intent word is heard (G6).
A badge may show an icon per intent beside its word, never alone, because the word is the status and the sign only strengthens it (G6).
The sort button of a table shows the direction as an icon, because an arrow says ascending or descending in one glance; aria-sort says it aloud.
The field of a select shows a chevron, because the sign says that a list opens below; the icon takes the field's size.
An icon that carries meaning may show its name as a tooltip, because the word confirms what the sign says; a decorative icon has none.
An entry of a menu may carry an icon before its word, because the sign is read faster than the word; the word names the action.
The summary of a disclosure shows a chevron that turns with the state, because the sign says that there is more and whether it is shown.
The arrows of a pagination are the icons chevron-left and chevron-right, because an arrow is a sign of the system that mirrors in right-to-left writing.
The separator of a breadcrumb is the icon chevron-right, decorative, because it points down the path.
The button of a file input shows the icon upload and its remove buttons the icon close, because the sign is read faster than the word; the word names the action.
